name: Sun
description: The Sun is the G-type main-sequence star at the center of our Solar System. Containing 99.86% of all mass in the solar system, nuclear fusion in its core converts hydrogen into helium at 15 million °C, powering light and thermal energy across space.
moons: Orbits 8 major planets & thousands of minor bodies

name: Moon
description: Earth's only natural satellite, formed 4.5 billion years ago from a giant impact. It is tidally locked to Earth, always showing the same hemisphere. Its surface is scarred by impact craters, maria (basaltic plains), and high lunar highlands.

name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun. Mercury experiences extreme temperature swings due to its thin exosphere. Its surface closely resembles Earth's Moon with heavy impact cratering and smooth volcanic plains.
best_viewing: Twilight immediately after sunset or before sunrise

name: Venus
description: Often called Earth's twin due to similar size and density, Venus is shrouded in thick clouds of sulfuric acid. A runaway greenhouse effect produces a crushing atmosphere 92 times Earth's pressure and surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead.
best_viewing: Evening Star or Morning Star near maximum elongation

name: Mars
description: The Red Planet gets its iconic reddish hue from abundant iron oxide on its surface. Mars features Olympus Mons (the largest volcano in the solar system) and Valles Marineris (a vast canyon system stretching over 4,000 km).

name: Jupiter
description: The gas giant Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with twice the mass of all other planets combined. Famous for its Great Red Spot—an anticyclonic storm larger than Earth—and vibrant swirling atmospheric bands.

name: Saturn
description: Renowned for its breathtaking ring system composed of billions of ice particles, rocky debris, and dust. Saturn is a gas giant with a density less than water, surrounded by complex storm belts and intriguing icy moons.

name: Sirius
description: Known as the Dog Star, Sirius A is the brightest star in Earth's night sky. Located in Canis Major, it is a binary star system twice as massive as the Sun with a dense white dwarf companion, Sirius B (The Pup).

name: Canopus
description: The second-brightest star in the night sky. A bright giant star of spectral type A9, Canopus is 10,000 times more luminous than our Sun and serves as a vital navigational beacon for spacecraft.

name: Arcturus
description: A red giant star in the constellation Boötes and the fourth-brightest star in the night sky. Arcturus has exhausted core hydrogen and expanded to 25 times the radius of the Sun.

name: Vega
description: The fifth-brightest star in the sky and a vertex of the Summer Triangle asterism. Vega was the first star other than the Sun to be photographed and boasts a prominent circumstellar dust disk.

name: Betelgeuse
description: A striking red supergiant star marking Orion's right shoulder. If placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would extend beyond Jupiter's orbit. Betelgeuse is expected to explode in a core-collapse supernova within 100,000 years.

name: Rigel
description: A brilliant blue supergiant star serving as Orion's left foot. Rigel shines with the luminosity of 120,000 Suns and illuminates neighboring dust clouds including the Witch Head Nebula.

name: Polaris
description: The famous North Star, currently positioned less than 1 degree from the northern celestial pole. Polaris is a multiple star system anchored by a yellow supergiant (Polaris Aa) used for orientation for centuries.

name: Orion Nebula
description: A vibrant diffuse star-forming region located south of Orion's Belt. Visible to the naked eye, M42 is one of the closest major stellar nurseries to Earth, containing hundreds of young protostars and the famous Trapezium Cluster.

name: Andromeda Galaxy
description: The nearest major spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, containing over 1 trillion stars. On a clear night, M31 appears as a faint smudge in Andromeda and is approaching our galaxy at 110 km/s, headed for a galactic collision in 4.5 billion years.
surface_temp: Galactic core stars ~4,000 K to 30,000 K

name: Pleiades
description: Also known as the Seven Sisters, the Pleiades is an open star cluster dominated by hot blue luminous B-type stars enveloped by a delicate reflection nebula.

name: Hercules Cluster
description: A magnificent globular star cluster in Hercules packing several hundred thousand ancient stars into a sphere roughly 145 light-years across. In 1974, the Arecibo message was beamed toward M13.
